excerpts.text: A route is an ordered list of stops. A label names one stop. A tag groups stops by a shared feature. Changing a label does not change the route order. Rearranging stops changes the route order. Two stops may share a tag while retaining different labels.

entries.title: Routes, labels and tags
entries.scope: Invented structural fixture. No real course materials or student trial were processed.

blocks.text: Order, naming and grouping answer different questions. A route fixes sequence; labels name individual stops; tags link stops by shared features. A rename preserves order, so first identify whether a task changes a name or a position before predicting the route.
A display filter changes which stops appear according to a selected tag. It leaves the stored order intact, just as renaming leaves order intact, although the two actions change different things.

The reading distinguishes hiding from deletion. This addresses the question in the personal notes: lack of visibility alone does not mean a stop was deleted. The note is a student question; the reading supplies the explanation.

blocks.prompt: Hypothetical route: North then South. Both stops have the tag quiet. Rename North to Oak without moving it. State the resulting order and whether sharing quiet makes the two stop labels identical.
blocks.answer: Oak then South. Their labels remain different despite the shared tag.
blocks.rationale: Renaming changes a label, not position, so the first stop is still first. A tag groups stops by feature; the handout explicitly permits shared tags with different labels. Confusing a shared tag with a shared label would erase this distinction.

blocks.prompt: Hypothetical stored route: North (quiet), South (busy). Rename North to Oak, then filter the display to quiet. State the visible stop, the stored route, and whether South was deleted.
blocks.answer: Visible: Oak. Stored route: Oak then South. South was hidden, not deleted.
blocks.rationale: Renaming changes the first label without reordering. The filter displays stops tagged quiet, so only Oak appears. The reading establishes that hidden stops remain stored; South therefore remains second.

blocks.text: Sorting algorithms are explicitly excluded by the invented scope.
blocks.nextStep: Keep sorting outside this assessment preparation unless the scope is explicitly revised.
